YouTube title seed: Salt Can Melt Road Ice Below 0°C
YouTube description seed: Dissolved road salt lowers water’s freezing point. Road crews can also wet the salt before spreading it so more stays on the pavement. Have you seen a truck spraying liquid as it spreads salt? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts

Suggested opening hook: Salt can melt ice below zero degrees Celsius.
Suggested opening display: Ice Melts Below Zero
Select one meaningful emphasis token from the final opening display copy.

Scene development:
contradiction: close low view of recognizable salt grains resting on icy asphalt with a small existing liquid patch. Treat it as an illustrative result, not a timed experiment or temperature measurement; no instant full-road melt.
clue: wider view establishes that frozen patches and a small liquid patch coexist. Do not show a heater or reveal pre-wetting equipment before the second reveal.
mechanism: practical close view of grains dissolving in a thin wet patch on the same asphalt. Explain the lower freezing point of salt water; avoid invented molecular diagrams, heat glow or a fake thermometer.
second_reveal: fact consequence; close rear view of maintenance equipment shows a liquid spray contacting the salt at the spinner before spreading. Clearly distinguish this pre-wetting from spraying a bare road ahead of a storm.
payoff: contextual winter-road view shows patchy clearing and maintenance activity; connect the chemistry and getting more salt to stay on the pavement without claiming the road is now universally safe.

Source-backed facts:
mechanism: Dissolved road salt lowers the freezing point of water, allowing ice to melt at some pavement temperatures below zero degrees Celsius.
consequence: MnDOT pre-wets salt with brine or other liquid deicers at the spreader spinner to reduce bounce and scatter, help salt adhere to pavement and start melting more quickly.
temperature: Road salt becomes less effective as pavement temperature falls; pavement temperature and air temperature can differ.

Factual boundaries:
Say zero degrees Celsius in narration; the title’s 0°C does not mean zero degrees Fahrenheit.
The salt must dissolve. Do not imply that it warms the road, instantly melts all ice or works effectively at every subzero temperature.
Do not use air temperature as proof of pavement temperature or invent a recorded temperature, concentration, melting time or fixed performance threshold.
Scope the pre-wetting example to MnDOT’s described equipment and practice. Pre-wetting salt at a spinner is distinct from applying brine directly to the road for anti-icing.
The second reveal is getting more salt to stay on the pavement, not a repetition of lowering the freezing point.
Do not depict driving on a supposedly guaranteed safe treated road or provide household chemical recipes.
